questions.q: The name of the curve described parametrically by the equations $x = t^{2} + t + 1, y = t^{2} - t + 1,$ is
questions.solution:
Here, we are having& $x = t^{2} + t + 1, y = t^{2} - t + 1,$

On subtracting~$y$~from~$x,$~we get

$x - y = t^{2} + t + 1 - \left(t^{2} - t + 1\right)$

$⇒ x - y = 2t$~or~$t = $\dfrac{x - y}{2},

On putting the value of~$t,$~in~$x,$~we get

$x = \left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right)2 + \$left(\dfrac{x - y}{2}\right) +$1,$

On further simplification, we get

$x = $\dfrac{x^{2} - 2xy + y^{2}}{4} + \dfrac{x - y}{2} +$1,$

$⇒ 4x = x^{2} - 2xy + y^{2} + 2x - 2y + 4,$

Final equation, we get as~$x^{2} - 2xy + y^{2} - 2x - 2y + 4 = 0,$

On comparing, this with the general equation of second degree, i.e.,~$ax^{2} + 2hxy + by^{2} + 2gx + 2fy + c = 0,$~

we will~get~$a = 1, h = - 1, b = 1, g = - 1, f = - 1, c = 4 .$

Now, to check for the type of conic, we will check

$∆ = abc + 2fgh - af^{2} - bg^{2} - ch^{2}$ and~$h^{2} - ab .$

$∆ = 4 - 2 - 1 - 1 - 4 = - 4 \ne 0,$

Now,~$h^{2} - ab = 1 - 1 = 0 .$

As, we are having~$∆ \ne 0$~and~$h^{2} - ab = 0,$ \text{ and } which is the condition for a parabola.

$

questions.q: If the line $y - 2 = 0$ is the directrix of the parabola ${x}^{2} - ky + 32 = 0, k \ne 0$ and the parabola intersects the circle ${x}^{2} + {y}^{2} = 8$ at two real distinct points, then the absolute value of $k$ is
questions.solution:
${x}^{2} - ky + 32 = 0$
$⇒ {x}^{2} = k\left(y - \dfrac{32}{k}\right)$
Put, $x = X, y - \dfrac{32}{k} = Y$
The equation of directrix is $Y + \dfrac{k}{4} = 0$
i.e. $y - \dfrac{32}{k} + \dfrac{k}{4} = 0$
But, $y - 2 = 0$ is the directrix.
$⇒ \dfrac{32}{k} - \dfrac{k}{4} = 2$
$⇒ {k}^{2} + 8k - 128 = 0$
$⇒ k = - 16$ or $k = 8$
For $k = 8,$ the parabola is ${x}^{2} = 8\left(y - 4\right)$ which does not intersect the circle.
For $k = - 16,$ the parabola is ${x}^{2} = - 16\left(y + 2\right)$ which intersects the circle at two real distinct points.
$⇒$ Absolute value of $k = \left|- 16\right| = 16$

questions.q: The value of& $\lambda$~for which the curve~\left(7x + 5\right)2 + \left(7y + 3\right)2 = {λ}^{2}\left(4x + 3y - 24\right)2$ \text{ and } represents a parabola, is$
questions.solution:
Given, curve is

\left(7x + 5\right)2 + \left(7y + 3\right)2 = {λ}^{2}\left(4x + 3y - 24\right)2,$

$⇒ \left\{7\left(x + \dfrac{5}{7}\right)\right\}2 + \left\{7\left(y + \dfrac{3}{7}\right)\right\}2 = {λ}^{2}\left\{\left(\sqrt{{4}^{2} + {3}^{2}}\right)2 \times \left(\dfrac{4x + 3y - 24}{{4}^{2} + {3}^{2}}\right)\right\}2,$

$⇒ 49\left[\left(x + \dfrac{5}{7}\right)2 + \left(y + \dfrac{3}{7}\right)2\right] = 25{λ}^{2}\left(\dfrac{4x + 3y - 24}{{4}^{2} + {3}^{2}}\right)2,$

$⇒ \left(x + \dfrac{5}{7}\right)2 + \left(y + \dfrac{3}{7}\right)2 = \dfrac{25{λ}^{2}}{49}\left(\dfrac{4x + 3y - 24}{{4}^{2} + {3}^{2}}\right)2,$

$⇒ \sqrt{\left(x + \dfrac{5}{7}\right)2 + \left(y + \dfrac{3}{7}\right)2} = \dfrac{5\left|\lambda\right|}{7} \times \left|\dfrac{4x + 3y - 24}{{4}^{2} + {3}^{2}}\right| .$

The $L . H . S .$~of the above equation represent distance of a point~ \left(x, y\right)$~from a point \left(- \dfrac{5}{7}, - \dfrac{3}{7}\right)$~and $R . H . S .$~represent its perpendicular distance from a line~$4x + 3y - 24 = 0 .$

Hence, the above equation satisfy the basic definition of a conic~section,~i.e.,~\left(PS\right) = e\left(PM\right),$~where~$PS$~is the distance of a variable point from a fixed point (focus) and~$PM$~is its perpendicular distance from a fixed line (directrix) and~$e$~is the eccentricity.

And, we know that, for parabola~$e = 1 .$

$∴ \left|\begin{array}{ll}\lambda\end{array}\right| = \dfrac{7}{5},$~$⇒ \lambda = \pm \dfrac{7}{5} .$

But $2 h=k$, then $k^{2}=16 h$ \begin{aligned} \Rightarrow & & 4 h^{2} &=16 h \\ \Rightarrow & & h &=0, h=4 \\ \Rightarrow & & k &=0, k=8 \end{aligned} $\therefore$ Points are $(0,0),(4,8)$. questions.solution:
Given parabola is& $y^{2} = 8x$

By comparing with parabola~$y^{2} = 4ax$

$a = 2$

Parametric point on parabola is~ \left(at^{2}, 2at\right) = \left(2t^{2}, 4t\right) = \left(\dfrac{1}{2},2\right)$

$⇒ 4t = 2$

$t = \dfrac{1}{2}$

Length of focal chord will be~a \left($t + $\dfrac{1}{t}\right)$2$

$= 2 $\$left(\dfrac{1}{2} +$2\right)2$

$= 2 \times \left(\dfrac{25}{4}\right)$

$= \dfrac{25}{2}$

$

questions.q: If the line $y = x - 1$ bisects two chords of the parabola $y^{2} = 4bx$ which are passing through the point \left(b, - 2b\right),$ then the length of the latus rectum can be equal to$
questions.solution:
Any point on $y = x – 1$ can be taken as \left(h, h – 1\right)$
Taking \left(h, h - 1\right)$ as the midpoint of chord, the equation of chord is $y\left(h - 1\right) - 4b\left(\dfrac{x + h}{2}\right) = { \left(h - 1\right)}^{2} - 4bh$
Which passes through the point \left(b, - 2b\right)$
$⇒- 2b\left(h - 1\right) - 2b\left(b + h\right) = h^{2} - 2h + 1 - 4bh$
$⇒h^{2} - 2h + \left(2b^{2} - 2b + 1\right) = 0$
As, above equation has two real roots, hence,
${\left(-$2\right)}^{2} - $4\left($1\right)\left(2b^{2} - 2b + 1\right) > 0$
$⇒2b^{2} - 2b < 0 ⇒ b < 1 ⇒ 4b < 4$
$⇒$ length of latus rectum is less than $4$

questions.q: The radius of the circle whose centre is$( - 4, 0 )$~and which cuts the parabola $y^{2} = 8x$ at $A$ and $B$, such that its common chord $AB$ subtends a right angle at the vertex of the parabola is equal to
questions.solution:
The centre of the circle is \left(- 4, 0\right)$~and let $r$ be the radius of the circle.

Then, we know that the equation of a circle with centre~ \left(h, k\right)$~and radius~$r$~is~\left(x - h\right)2 + \left(y - k\right)2 = r^{2}$~

Using this the equation of the circle is $( x + 4{)}^{2} + y^{2} = r^{2} .$

This cuts the parabola~at points $A \left({x}_{1}, {y}_{1}\right)$and $B \left({x}_{2}, {y}_{2}\right)

Then, we can find the~abscissa~of $A$ and $B$~by putting the value~$y^{2} = 8x$~from the parabola~to the circle.

Hence, we get an~equation \text{ and } $( x + 4{)}^{2} + 8x = r^{2},$

~$⇒ x^{2} + 8x + 16 + 8x = r^{2}$

$⇒ x^{2} + 16x + 16 - r^{2} = 0 .$

The roots of this equation are~${x}_{1}$~and~${x}_{2}$,~hence~sum of the roots is~${x}_{1} + {x}_{2} = - \dfrac{16}{1} = -16$~and product of roots is~${x}_{1}{x}_{2} = \dfrac{16 - r^{2}}{1} =16 - r^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

The co-ordinates of $A$ and $B$ are given by ${y}_{1}^{2} = 8{x}_{1}$ and ${y}_{2}^{2} = 8{x}_{2}$~respectively.

$∴ {y}_{1} = \pm2\sqrt{2}{x}_{1}$~and ${y}_{2} = \$pm2\sqrt{2}{x}_{2} .

Since, $AB$ subtends a right angle at the vertex of the parabola.

$∴ {m}_{OA} \cdot {m}_{OB} = -1$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{{y}_{1} - 0}{{x}_{1} - 0}\right)\left(\dfrac{{y}_{2} - 0}{{x}_{2} - 0}\right) = -1$

$∴ \dfrac{y1}{x1} \times \dfrac{y2}{x2} = -1$~$⇒ {x}_{1}{x}_{2} + {y}_{1}{y}_{2} = 0$

But,~${y}_{1} = \$pm2\sqrt{2}{x}_{1}~and~${y}_{2} = \pm2\sqrt{2}{x}_{2}$

$⇒ {x}_{1}{x}_{2} + \left(\$pm2\sqrt{2}{x}_{1}\right)\left(\ppm2\sqrt{2}{x}_{2}\right) =0$~

$⇒ {x}_{1}{x}_{2} + 8{x}_{1}{x}_{2} = 0$

$⇒ {x}_{1}{x}_{2} = 0$~

On putting the value of~${x}_{1}{x}_{2}$~from equation~\left(1\right),$~we get

$16 - r^{2} = 0⇒ r = 4 .$

The radius of the circle is equal to the absolute value of the~$x -$co-ordinate of the centre, hence the circle touches the~$Y -$axis at origin.

Hence, it also touches the parabola and will not intersect it at any point, so no such circle exist.

$

questions.q: Find the equation to the parabola, whose axis parallel to the $y$-axis and which passes through the points $(0,4),(1,9)$ and $(4,5)$ is
questions.solution:
The equation of parabola parallel to $y$-axis is
$y=A x^2+B x+C$ ...(i)
The point $(0,4),(1,9)$ and $(4,5)$ lies on Eq. (i). Then, $\quad 4=0+0+C \Rightarrow C=4$ ...(ii)
$9=A+B+C$
or $\quad 9=A+B+4 \quad(\because C=4)A+B=5$ ...(iii)
and $\quad 5=16 A+4 B+C \quad(\because C=4)$
or $\quad 5=16 A+4 B+4\therefore \quad 16 A+4 B=14 A+B=\frac{1}{4}$ ...(iv)
Solving Eqs. (iii) and (iv),
we get $\quad A=\frac{-19}{12}, B=\frac{79}{12}$ ...(v)
Substituting the values of $A, B$ and $C$ from Eqs. (ii) and (v) in Eq. (i), then equation of parabola is
$y=\frac{-19}{12} x^2+\frac{79}{12} x+4$

questions.q: If the focal chord drawn through the point $(1,2)$ to the parabola $y^2=8 x$ meets this parabola in  \left(x_1, y_1\right)$ and  \left(x_2, y_2\right)$ then $x_1+x_2=$
questions.solution:
Given parabola is $\mathrm{y}^2=8 \mathrm{x}$ with parametric coordinates \left(\mathrm{at}_1^2, 2 \mathrm{at}{ }_1\right)$ and \left(\mathrm{at}_2^2, 2 \mathrm{at}_2\right)$. $\operatorname{Let} \left(\mathrm{x}_1, \mathrm{y}_1\right) \rightarrow\left(a \mathrm{t}_1^2, 2 a t_1\right)$ and \left(\mathrm{x}_2, \mathrm{y}_2\right) \rightarrow\left(a t_2^2, 2 a t_2\right)$ Equation of line passing through \left(\mathrm{x}_1, \mathrm{y}_1\right) \text { and }\left(\mathrm{x}_2, \mathrm{y}_2\right) \text { is }\left(\mathrm{y}-2 \mathrm{at}_1\right)
\begin{aligned}$& $=\frac{2 a t_2-2 a t_1}{a t_2^2-a t_1^2}\left($x-a t_1^2\right) \\ & \left(y-2 a t_1\$right)=\frac{2}{\left(t_2+t_1\right)}\left($x-a t_1^2\right)\end{aligned}$ Satisfy $(1,2)$, \begin{aligned} & \left(2-2 a t_1\right)=\frac{2}{\left(t_2+t_1\right)}\left(1-a t_1^2\right) \\ & \left(1-a_1\right)=\frac{1}{\left(t_2+t_1\right)}\left(1-a_1^2\right) \\ & \left(1-a t_1\right)\left(t_2+t_1\right)=\left(1-a t_1^2\right) \\ & \mathrm{t}_2+t_1-\mathrm{at}_1 \mathrm{t}_2-\mathrm{at}_1^2=1-\mathrm{at}_1^2 \end{aligned} Here foci $a=2$.
When satisfy foci coordinates $(a, 0)$ then the required equation gives the relation $t_1 t_2=-1$ From (i) $\begin{aligned}$ \text{ and } \mathrm{t}_2+\mathrm{t}_1-2(-1)=1 \\ \text{ and } \mathrm{t}_2+\mathrm{t}_1+2=1 \end{aligned}
$\begin{aligned}$ \text{ and } \mathrm{x}_1+\mathrm{x}_2=a \mathrm{t}_1^2+a \mathrm{t}_2^2 \\ \text{ and } =\mathrm{a}\left[\mathrm{t}_1^2+\mathrm{t}_2^2+2 \mathrm{t}_1 \mathrm{t}_2-2 \mathrm{t}_1 \mathrm{t}_2\right] \\ \text{ and } =\mathrm{a}\left[\left(\mathrm{t}_1+\mathrm{t}_2\right)^2-2 \mathrm{t}_1 \mathrm{t}_2\right] \\ \text{ and } =2\left[(-1)^2-2(-1)\right] \\ \text{ and } =[1+2]=2 \times 3=6 \end{aligned} So, option (c) is correct.

(ii) is $(0,0)$. $\begin{array}{cc} \therefore$ \text{ and }  X=0, Y=0 \\ \Rightarrow  \text{ and }  x-y=0, x+y+3=0 \\ \Rightarrow  \text{ and }  x=-$\frac{3}{2},$y=$\frac{-3}{2} \end{array}

questions.solution:
For a focal chord of parabola ${t}_{1}{t}_{2} = - 1$,where ${t}_{1}$and ${t}_{2}$~are parameters of two ends of the focal chord. Since one end is given~$t$~, then value of the parameter for the other end of the focal chord is $= - \dfrac{1}{t}$

$∴  $The co-ordinates of the end points of the focal chords are \left(at^{2}, 2at\right)$~and \left(\dfrac{a}{t2},\dfrac{- 2a}{t}\right)$

$∴  $Length of the focal chord $=\sqrt{\left(at^{2} - \dfrac{a}{t2}\right)2 + \left(2at + \dfrac{2a}{t}\right)2}$

$= a\sqrt{t^{4} + \dfrac{1}{t4} - 2 + 4t^{2} + \dfrac{4}{t2} + 8}$

$= a\sqrt{t^{4} + \dfrac{1}{t4} + 4t^{2} + \dfrac{4}{t2} + 6} = a\sqrt{\left(t^{2} + \dfrac{1}{t2} + 2\right)2}$

$= a\left(t^{2} + \dfrac{1}{t2} + 2\right) = a\left(t + \dfrac{1}{t}\right)2$

Let, \left(h, k\right)$ be the coordinates of the centre of the circle described on $PQ$ as diameter. Then,
$h = \dfrac{a}{2} \left({t}_{1}^{2} + {t}_{2}^{2}\right)$and $k = a \left({t}_{1} + {t}_{2}\right)

$⇒ \dfrac{2h}{a} = {t}_{1}^{2} + {t}_{2}^{2}$and $\dfrac{k^{2}}{a^{2}} = {t}_{1}^{2} + {t}_{2}^{2} +2{t}_{1}{t}_{2}$
$⇒ \dfrac{k^{2}}{a^{2}} = \dfrac{2h}{a} -2 \left[$∵ {t}_{1}{t}_{2} = - 1\right]$
$⇒ k^{2} = 2a \left($h - a\right)$
Hence, the locus of \left($h, k\right)$ is
$y^{2} = $2a\left($x - a\right) .$

questions.q: The axis of a parabola is along the line $y = x$~and the distance of its vertex~$A$ from  \left(0, 0\right)$~is $\sqrt{2}$ and that of its focus~$S$ from  \left(0, 0\right)$~is $2\sqrt{2}$. If~$A$ and~$S$ lie in first quadrant, then the equation of the parabola in parametric form is
questions.solution:
Distance of vertex from origin $= \sqrt{2}$

Distance of focus from origin $= 2\sqrt{2}$

Axis is along $y = x$. The focus and the vertex lie in the first quadrant.

Hence, the coordinates of the focus are \left(2, 2\right)$.

The vertex is at \left(1, 1\right)$

Hence, the equation of directrix is $x + y = 0$

Take point \left(h, k\right)$ on the parabola.

By definition of the parabola

\left(h - 2\right)2 + \left(k - 2\right)2 = \left|\dfrac{h + k}{2}\right|2$

$⇒ 2h^{2} + 2k^{2} + 16 - 8h - 8k = h^{2} + k^{2} + 2hk$

$⇒ h^{2} + k^{2} - 8h - 8k - 2hk + 16 = 0$

Substitute \left(h, k\right)$ to \left(x, y\right)$

$x^{2} + y^{2} - 2xy - 8x - 8y + 16 = 0$

This is the equation of parabola.

\left(x - y\right)2 = 8 \left(x + y - 2\right)$

So,~$x = \left(t + 1\right)2$~and~$y = \left(t - 1\right)2$~satisfies above equation, therefore option~\left(A\right)& is correct.

$

questions.q: Through the vertex $\text{O}$~of the parabola $y^{2} = 4ax$~chords~$\text{OP}$ and~$\text{OQ}$ are drawn such that $\text{OP}$~is perpendicular to $\text{OQ}$. For each and every possible chords~$\text{OP}$ and $\text{OQ}$, the chord $\text{PQ}$& cuts the axis of parabola at a fixed point, whose coordinates are&
questions.solution:
Given parabola is $y^{2} = 4ax$.

Any point on the above parabola can be assumed as $( at^{2}, 2at )$.

Let us assume that the coordinates of points $P$ and $Q$~are $P \left(a{t}_{1}^{2}, 2a{t}_{1}\right)$~and $Q \left(a{t}_{2}^{2}, 2a{t}_{2}\right)$.

Therefore, slope of $OP = \dfrac{2a{t}_{1} - 0}{a{t}_{1}^{2} - 0} = \dfrac{2}{t1}$

and slope of $OQ = \dfrac{2a{t}_{2} - 0}{a{t}_{2}^{2} - 0} = \dfrac{2}{t2}$

Since, $OP ⊥ OQ$, hence $\dfrac{2}{t1} \times \dfrac{2}{t2} = -1$

$⇒ {t}_{1}{t}_{2} = - 4$

Also, the equation of the chord joining $P$ and $Q$~is,

$y - 2a{t}_{1} = \dfrac{2a{t}_{2} - 2a{t}_{1}}{a{t}_{2}^{2} - a{t}_{1}^{2}} \left(x - a{t}_{1}^{2}\right)$

$⇒ y\left({t}_{1} + {t}_{2}\right) =2x + 2a{t}_{1}{t}_{2}$

Now,~${t}_{1}{t}_{2} = - 4$

The equation of $PQ$is $y\left({t}_{1} + {t}_{2}\right) =2x + 2a{t}_{1}{t}_{2}$

$∴ y\left({t}_{1} + {t}_{2}\right) =2x - 8a$

$⇒ \left({t}_{1} + {t}_{2}\right)\left(y - 0\right) - 2\left(x - 4a\right) = 0$

The above line always passes through the point of intersection of $y = 0$ and $x = 4a$ i.e., the fixed point is $( 4a, 0 ).

$

The equation of parabola parallel to $y$-axis is
$y=A x^2+B x+C$ ...(i)

$9=A+B+C$
or $\quad 9=A+B+4 \quad(\because C=4)A+B=5$ ...(iii)
and $\quad 5=16 A+4 B+C \quad(\because C=4)$
or $\quad 5=16 A+4 B+4\therefore \quad 16 A+4 B=14 A+B=\frac{1}{4}$ ...(iv)
Solving Eqs. (iii) and (iv),
we get $\quad A=\frac{-19}{12}, B=\frac{79}{12}$ ...(v)
Substituting the values of $A, B$ and $C$ from Eqs. (ii) and (v) in Eq. (i), then equation of parabola is
$y=\frac{-19}{12} x^2+\frac{79}{12} x+4$

questions.q: Slope of the chord of parabola $y^{2} = 4ax$ which passes through the point~  \left(- 6a, 0\right)$ and which subtends an angle of~$45 °$ at the vertex, is$
questions.solution:
Given& parabola& $y^{2} = 4ax$.

Focus lies at~ \left(a, 0\right)$~and vertex lies at~ \left(0, 0\right)$.

Now, equation of chord passing through given point is~$y = m ( x + 6a )$

$⇒ \dfrac{y - mx}{6am} = 1$

Homogenizing it with the parabola,~$y^{2} - 4ax\left(\dfrac{y - mx}{6am}\right) = 0$

$⇒ 4amx^{2} + 6amy^{2} - 4axy = 0$

It is given that chord subtends~$45 °$~angle at origin. Therefore,~

$tan ⁡ {45}^{o} = \left|\dfrac{2\sqrt{4a^{2} - 24a^{2}m^{2}}}{4am + 6am}\right|$

$⇒ 100a^{2}m^{2} = 4 \left(4a^{2} - 24a^{2}m^{2}\right)$

$⇒ 49m^{2} = 4$

$⇒ m = \pm \dfrac{2}{7}$

$
